name: Amantadine

lead: Amantadine began as a flu drug in the 1960s and turned out to help Parkinson's symptoms. Today it is mostly a neurological medicine, including for recovery after brain injury.
People interested in energy and motivation talk about it because it raises dopamine activity, which they connect to training drive.

paras: It increases dopamine release, blocks NMDA glutamate receptors and has mild anticholinergic action. Against flu it blocks the M2 proton channel.

The label lists nausea, dizziness, insomnia, hallucinations, livedo reticularis and low blood pressure on standing. Overdose deaths are documented, especially with kidney impairment. Prescription-only.

angle.text: People discuss amantadine as a dopamine-boosting option for fatigue and motivation, which they link to training consistency and appearance. It is a prescription drug used mainly for Parkinson's disease and brain injury.

lead: Amantadine is an oral prescription drug that increases dopamine signalling and blocks NMDA glutamate receptors. It was first approved in the US in 1966 for influenza A and later became a Parkinson's disease medicine [1][2]. In recovery and focus discussions it is known as a dopaminergic drug that has also been used for brain-injury recovery, fatigue and low motivation, which people connect with energy, training drive and presentation.

The US label lists indications for influenza A prophylaxis and treatment and for parkinsonism and drug-induced extrapyramidal reactions [3]. Because many circulating influenza strains became resistant, antiviral guidance no longer recommends it for flu, and its main role is neurological [4][5]. Extended-release forms were later approved for levodopa-induced dyskinesia [1].

A multicentre randomised trial of 184 patients with severe traumatic brain injury in a vegetative or minimally conscious state reported faster functional recovery on amantadine than placebo over the treatment period [6]. Registered trials have also tested it for post-COVID fatigue and cognition, cerebral palsy and gait in Parkinson's disease [7][8][9][10].

paras: Against influenza A, amantadine blocks the viral M2 proton channel and so prevents viral uncoating [11][12]. In the nervous system its effects are less fully described and involve enhanced dopamine release, NMDA receptor antagonism and mild anticholinergic action [1].

Approved uses are influenza A and parkinsonism [3]. Reviews cover its place among Parkinson's treatments [2] and among options for dementia with Lewy bodies [13]. Systematic reviews of agitation after traumatic brain injury discuss it among the agents studied [14]. Disorders-of-consciousness guidelines address amantadine after brain injury [15].

Beyond the 2012 brain-injury trial [6], early reports examined amantadine in depression and migraine in 1971 and 1972 [16][17]. Recent trials include extended-release amantadine for OFF-related dystonia [18] and post-COVID fatigue [10][1].

The label lists nausea, dizziness and insomnia as most frequent (5-10%), with hallucinations, confusion, livedo reticularis, orthostatic hypotension and others less often [3]. Deaths have been reported from overdose, particularly with kidney impairment [3]. Animal studies showed embryonic toxicity at high doses [3].
